plan.title: RSEM colon treated vs control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, human colon) summarized from RSEM expected counts, with metadata declaring 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. The per-sample RSEM genes.results files carrying effective lengths were not delivered, so the tximport(type='rsem') offset path that would normally be used for RSEM quantifications cannot run here; the plan instead rounds the delivered expected-count matrix to nearest integers and documents this as a stated deviation, since DESeq2/edgeR require integer counts. Sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the study median, a fact the plan carries through QC rather than dropping silently, per the rule that a low-depth sample is down-weighted by its size factor and removed only for a stated reason from structure QC, not for depth alone. The flow is: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to inspect sample_01 and make an explicit keep/drop call; (2) DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage as the primary differential expression test, with an explicit reference level (control), minimal pre-filter, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and outlier/NA reporting; (3) an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as a robustness cross-check, since 6 replicates/group sits inside the range where the two tools can disagree, reporting the overlap as the high-confidence set; (4) fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (human) as the primary collection, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways (human) as secondary collections, each reported with its own version and FDR, without merging sets across collections; (5) a consolidated report with fit diagnostics, the QC decision on sample_01, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record.
